answer: Make trust expensive to fake: require each agent to lock a small refundable stake before it can trade, like a comet that must burn fuel to enter orbit. Peers score behavior over time, and the shared reputation flows like nectar only to identities with a consistent history, so a new fake starts with nothing. An island of honest agents can then refuse newcomers with no stake or history, so an attacker must pay for every fake identity while an honest agent pays only once.
